spec.title: State of charge (SoC)
spec.description: Battery state of charge and daily net consumption/production

spec.rawSql:
SELECT
  day,
  (SUM(avg_energy_per_pack) / NULLIF(SUM(avg_energy_per_pack / NULLIF(avg_soc_per_pack, 0) * 100), 0)) * 100 AS soc
FROM (
  SELECT
    date_bin(INTERVAL '1 day', ts) AS day,
    topic,
    AVG(energy)                    AS avg_energy_per_pack,
    AVG(soc)                       AS avg_soc_per_pack
  FROM views.slv_batteries
  WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  AND num_connected_strings > 0
  GROUP BY day, topic
)
GROUP BY day

SELECT *
FROM (
  WITH
  start_value AS (
    SELECT
      day AS start_day,
      AVG(total_soc) as start_soc
    FROM (
      SELECT
        date_trunc('day', hour) AS day,
        SUM(soc) AS total_soc
      FROM energy.electrical_soc_hourly
      WHERE hour BETWEEN to_date('$start_date', 'DD Mon YYYY') AND to_date('$start_date', 'DD Mon YYYY') + TIME '23:59'
      GROUP BY hour
    )
    GROUP BY day
  ),
  future AS (
    SELECT
      (start_day + n * INTERVAL '1 day')::date AS day,
      start_soc - $daily_consumption * n AS soc
    FROM start_value
    CROSS JOIN generate_series(0, 30) AS n
  )
  SELECT
    day AS time,
    soc * 100 / $max_soc AS soc_prediction
  FROM future
)
ORDER BY time

WITH
  start_point AS (
    SELECT
      day::date AS start_day,
      AVG(total_soc) as start_soc
    FROM (
      SELECT
        date_trunc('day', hour) AS day,
        SUM(soc) AS total_soc
      FROM energy.electrical_soc_hourly
      WHERE hour BETWEEN to_date('$start_date', 'DD Mon YYYY') AND to_date('$start_date', 'DD Mon YYYY') + TIME '23:59'
      GROUP BY hour
    )
    GROUP BY day
  ),
  end_point AS (
    SELECT
      day::date AS end_day,
      AVG(total_soc) as end_soc
    FROM (
      SELECT
        date_trunc('day', hour) AS day,
        SUM(soc) AS total_soc
      FROM energy.electrical_soc_hourly
      WHERE hour >= (SELECT date_trunc('day', MAX(hour)) FROM energy.electrical_soc_hourly)
      GROUP BY hour
    )
    GROUP BY day
  ),
  consumption_values AS (
    SELECT 
      s.start_day AS start_date,
      e.end_day AS end_date,
      s.start_soc AS start_value,
      (e.end_soc - s.start_soc) / GREATEST(1, (e.end_day - s.start_day)) AS daily_consumption
    FROM start_point s
    CROSS JOIN end_point e
  )
SELECT
  (start_date + n * INTERVAL '1 day')::date AS day,
  CASE WHEN start_date = end_date
    THEN NULL
    ELSE (start_value + n * daily_consumption) * 100 / $max_soc
  END AS soc_calculated
FROM consumption_values
CROSS JOIN generate_series(0, 30) AS n

WITH start AS (
  SELECT $__from / 1000 AS start_date
)
SELECT
  to_timestamp(start_date + n * 86400)::DATE AS day,
  $min_soc AS soc_threshold
FROM start
CROSS JOIN (
  SELECT unnest(generate_series(0, 100, 1)) AS n
) AS series

SELECT
  date_trunc('day',  hour) DAY,
  CASE WHEN SUM(-energy_wh) > 0 THEN SUM(-energy_wh)
  ELSE NULL END AS daily_consumption,
  CASE WHEN SUM(energy_wh) > 0 THEN SUM(energy_wh)
  ELSE NULL END AS daily_production
FROM energy.electrical_hourly
GROUP BY DAY
ORDER BY DAY desc

spec.title: Total electrical energy consumption and production

spec.rawSql:
-- Energy per main group and sub group per day, in Wh: the base query of this dashboard; the other
-- panels reuse its result. Each source is filtered on its raw time and averaged per device and day, and
-- only then joined to its metadata; the series that combine signals are sums and differences of those averages.
-- Energy is the average power × the part of the day inside the time range and before now. group_energy
-- is a main group's energy over the whole range (the treemap's colour). Each view is read once: a row that counts
-- in two series is repeated with a role (CROSS JOIN VALUES), as Greptime runs a CTE again for every reference.
-- See zero-data/docs/energy-dashboard-model.md.
WITH
-- Devices whose groups are fixed: shore, shore converter losses, solar, thrusters, chiller, 350 VDC
fixed AS (
  SELECT date_bin('1 day'::INTERVAL, ts) AS time, main_group, sub_group, device, avg(power) AS power
  FROM views.gld_fixed_group_power
  WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  GROUP BY time, main_group, sub_group, device
),

-- Power tags: their own group, and subtracted from the grid converters' AC output as AC unallocated
tag AS (
  SELECT t.time, m.main_group, m.sub_group, t.power
  FROM (
    SELECT date_bin('1 day'::INTERVAL, ts) AS time, topic, avg(active_power_total) AS power
    FROM views.slv_power_tags
    WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
    GROUP BY time, topic
  ) AS t
  JOIN public.power_tag_metadata AS m ON t.topic = m.topic
  WHERE m.main_group IS NOT NULL AND m.excluded IS NOT TRUE
),

-- Grid converters: their AC output for AC unallocated, and DC input minus AC output as their loss
grid AS (
  SELECT
    date_bin('1 day'::INTERVAL, ts) AS time,
    converter,
    avg(CASE WHEN side = 'dc' THEN power END) AS dc_power,
    avg(CASE WHEN side = 'ac' THEN power END) AS ac_power
  FROM views.slv_grid_converters
  WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
  GROUP BY time, converter
),

-- 24 VDC power supplies: their output power per converter group, for 24VDC unallocated and the ring
dc_24v_supply AS (
  SELECT s.time, m.converter, sum(s.power) AS power
  FROM (
    SELECT date_bin('1 day'::INTERVAL, ts) AS time, topic, avg(power) AS power
    FROM views.slv_24vdc_power_supplies
    WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
    GROUP BY time, topic
  ) AS s
  JOIN public.dc_24v_metadata AS m ON s.topic = m.topic
  WHERE m.converter IS NOT NULL AND m.converter_subnr IS NOT NULL
  GROUP BY s.time, m.converter
),

-- 24 VDC breakers: current × their converter's voltage (the first supply with a valid voltage, else 24 V). Their
-- own group, and subtracted from the supplies' output as 24VDC unallocated
dc_24v_breaker AS (
  SELECT c.time, m.main_group, m.sub_group, c.current * coalesce(v.voltage, 24.0) / 1000.0 AS power
  FROM (
    SELECT date_bin('1 day'::INTERVAL, ts) AS time, topic, avg(output_current) AS current
    FROM views.slv_24vdc_currents
    WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
    GROUP BY time, topic
  ) AS c
  JOIN public.dc_24v_metadata AS m ON c.topic = m.topic
  LEFT JOIN (
    SELECT
      s.time,
      m.converter,
      coalesce(
        avg(CASE WHEN m.converter_subnr = 1 THEN s.voltage END),
        avg(CASE WHEN m.converter_subnr = 2 THEN s.voltage END),
        avg(CASE WHEN m.converter_subnr = 3 THEN s.voltage END)
      ) AS voltage
    FROM (
      SELECT date_bin('1 day'::INTERVAL, ts) AS time, topic, avg(voltage) AS voltage
      FROM views.slv_24vdc_converter_voltages
      WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
      GROUP BY time, topic
    ) AS s
    JOIN public.dc_24v_metadata AS m ON s.topic = m.topic
    WHERE m.converter IS NOT NULL AND m.converter_subnr IS NOT NULL
    GROUP BY s.time, m.converter
  ) AS v ON v.time = c.time AND v.converter = m.converter
  WHERE m.converter IS NOT NULL AND m.main_group IS NOT NULL
),

-- 700 VDC ring: per segment, the flow in through its DC switches minus what its measured sources take. Each
-- switch counts for the segment on both sides; a bucket counts when all 8 switches have data in it.
ring_switch AS (
  SELECT time, technical_name, power, count(*) OVER (PARTITION BY time) AS switches
  FROM (
    SELECT date_bin('1 day'::INTERVAL, ts) AS time, technical_name, avg(power) AS power
    FROM views.slv_dc_ring_switches
    WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
    GROUP BY time, technical_name
  ) AS s
),
ring_segment AS (
  SELECT time, segment, sum(power) AS power
  FROM (
    SELECT
      s.time,
      CASE side.k WHEN 1 THEN m.downstream_segment ELSE m.upstream_segment END AS segment,
      CASE side.k WHEN 1 THEN m.sign * s.power ELSE -m.sign * s.power END AS power,
      s.switches
    FROM ring_switch AS s
    JOIN public.dc_ring_switch_metadata AS m ON s.technical_name = m.technical_name
    CROSS JOIN (VALUES (1), (2)) AS side(k)
    UNION ALL
    SELECT u.time, m.segment, -u.power, NULL
    FROM (
      SELECT time, kind, unit, sum(power) AS power
      FROM (
        SELECT date_bin('1 day'::INTERVAL, ts) AS time, kind, unit, device, avg(power) AS power
        FROM views.slv_dc_ring_sources
        WHERE $__timeFilter(ts)
        GROUP BY time, kind, unit, device
      ) AS d
      GROUP BY time, kind, unit
    ) AS u
    JOIN public.dc_ring_source_metadata AS m ON u.kind = m.kind AND u.unit = m.unit
    UNION ALL
    SELECT s.time, m.segment, -s.power, NULL
    FROM dc_24v_supply AS s
    JOIN public.dc_ring_source_metadata AS m ON m.kind = 'dc_24v_converter' AND s.converter = m.unit
  ) AS f
  GROUP BY time, segment
  HAVING max(switches) = 8
),

-- Every series. A series with an anchor (AC unallocated: the grid converters' AC output; 24VDC unallocated:
-- the supplies' output) only counts in the buckets where its anchor has data: anchor is 1 for those rows,
-- 0 for the rows subtracted from them, and NULL for every other series.
power AS (
  SELECT time, main_group, sub_group, power, NULL AS anchor FROM fixed
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    t.time,
    CASE r.k WHEN 1 THEN t.main_group ELSE 'Technical' END,
    CASE r.k WHEN 1 THEN t.sub_group ELSE 'AC unallocated' END,
    CASE r.k WHEN 1 THEN t.power ELSE -t.power END,
    CASE r.k WHEN 1 THEN NULL ELSE 0 END
  FROM tag AS t CROSS JOIN (VALUES (1), (2)) AS r(k)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    g.time,
    CASE r.k WHEN 1 THEN 'Technical' ELSE 'Losses' END,
    CASE r.k WHEN 1 THEN 'AC unallocated' ELSE 'Grid converters' END,
    CASE r.k WHEN 1 THEN g.ac_power ELSE g.dc_power - g.ac_power END,
    CASE r.k WHEN 1 THEN 1 END
  FROM grid AS g CROSS JOIN (VALUES (1), (2)) AS r(k)
  WHERE g.ac_power IS NOT NULL AND (r.k = 1 OR g.dc_power IS NOT NULL)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT
    b.time,
    CASE r.k WHEN 1 THEN b.main_group ELSE 'Technical' END,
    CASE r.k WHEN 1 THEN b.sub_group ELSE '24VDC unallocated' END,
    CASE r.k WHEN 1 THEN b.power ELSE -b.power END,
    CASE r.k WHEN 1 THEN NULL ELSE 0 END
  FROM dc_24v_breaker AS b CROSS JOIN (VALUES (1), (2)) AS r(k)
  UNION ALL
  SELECT time, 'Technical', '24VDC unallocated', power, 1
  FROM dc_24v_supply
  UNION ALL
  SELECT s.time, m.main_group, m.sub_group, s.power, NULL
  FROM ring_segment AS s
  JOIN public.dc_ring_segment_metadata AS m ON s.segment = m.segment
  WHERE m.main_group IS NOT NULL
)
,

energy AS (
  SELECT
    time,
    main_group,
    coalesce(sub_group, main_group) AS sub_group,
    sum(power) * (
      least(to_unixtime(time) + 86400, to_unixtime($__toTime), to_unixtime(now()))
      - greatest(to_unixtime(time), to_unixtime($__fromTime))
    ) / 3600.0 AS energy
  FROM power
  GROUP BY time, main_group, coalesce(sub_group, main_group)
  HAVING count(anchor) = 0 OR max(anchor) = 1
)

SELECT
  time,
  main_group,
  sub_group,
  energy,
  sum(energy) OVER (PARTITION BY main_group) AS group_energy
FROM energy
ORDER BY time, main_group, sub_group

spec.title: Total electrical energy consumption
spec.description: Total energy consumption per group and sub group

links.title: Range: ${range_warning}
links.tooltip: ${range_warning:text}. Click to show the last 30 days.

spec.rawSql:
SELECT date_format(day, '%Y_%m %d %m %Y') AS day
FROM (
  SELECT date_bin(INTERVAL '1 day', ts) AS day
  FROM views.slv_batteries
  WHERE ts > now() - INTERVAL '15 days'
  GROUP BY day
)
ORDER BY day DESC

spec.name: daily_consumption
spec.label: Daily consumption (kWh)
spec.description: The first element is the calculated daily consumption. Select any other value to evaluate a different scenario.

spec.name: range_warning
spec.description: For the Range link: 'ok', or a warning when the time range is longer than 30 days (value), and an explanation (text).

spec.__legacyStringValue:
-- For the Range link: a warning when the time range is longer than 30 days. The panels read the raw data of
-- the whole range, so a long range is slow and loads Zero's Greptime. The value is the link's status ("ok" or
-- "⚠️ 45 days"), the text its tooltip. Reads no table. The GreptimeDB plugin takes the first column as the
-- value and the second as the text, whatever their names.
SELECT
  CASE WHEN days > 30 THEN '⚠️ ' || cast(days AS STRING) || ' days' ELSE 'ok' END AS __value,
  CASE
    WHEN days > 30 THEN cast(days AS STRING) || ' days is over 30: the panels read the raw data of the whole range, about 75 s for 30 days and 2.5 min for 60'
    ELSE cast(days AS STRING) || ' days: up to 30 days loads in about a minute or less'
  END AS __text
FROM (
  SELECT cast(round((to_unixtime($__toTime) - to_unixtime($__fromTime)) / 86400.0) AS BIGINT) AS days
)
